$comment: Code Puppy authority registry (#1662 L4; coordinator instruction 2026-11-09: 'every decision Code Puppy makes today must still be Code Puppy's after the OpenCode 2 switch').

One entry per decision. Held entries name the OpenCode 2 mechanism file and the tests that turn red when the mechanism is removed; blocked entries carry the reason and the options awaiting the orchestrator.

An entry is never deleted: retiring one needs `retired: { quote, date, by }` with the owner's words. Judge: packages/ext/src/policy/authority-registry.test.ts (coverage of the 49 pre-switch takeovers, files and test names exist, no blocked entry, no deletion).

entries.note: Slice E (I-05 lane, 2026-11-12; design review reproduced it with the real bundled manifest): a tool registered under an MCP server's namespace by anyone other than that server's MCP layer must not borrow the server's identity or authority. Held at two ends: the project-plugin fan-out refuses a tool whose namespace is a configured MCP server's or a reserved one (opencode, codepuppy, codepuppy-*), logged in the ADR-041 refusal format (packages/ext/src/plugin-fanout.ts); and identity.ts gives a bundled Office server's namespace only to the tools its attested manifest declares — any other tool there is a plugin tool of unknown origin, not asserted. Residual, not closed: the plugin API (promise adapter tool list, Mcp.Server) carries no fact about which layer registered a tool, so a host-loaded plugin (outside the fan-out) can still register under a codepuppy-cloud or third-party server's namespace, or under a declared Office tool name, and receive that server's identity; closing it needs a fact minted by the MCP layer (packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts) that a plugin cannot write — reported to the orchestrator.

publishes the target's replied event first, then the cascaded ones

entries.note: Known red by design (orchestrator ruling 2026-11-12, option 甲: not taken over). Upstream tests asserting that an always reply writes a project-level saved approval: packages/core/test/permission.test.ts "stores and removes saved resources for a project" and the seven "<fixture>: always allow covers repeat execution and narrows prefix scope" cases (numeric npm script prefix, numeric AWS option prefix, substitution prefix, redirect prefix, assignment redirect prefix, PowerShell method prefix, PowerShell tab prefix); packages/core/test/tool-shell.test.ts "declarations reuse approvals while substitutions retain reject/once/always behavior"; packages/server/test/permission-saved.test.ts "edits saved permissions through PATCH". Reproduce: cd packages/core && bun test test/permission.test.ts test/tool-shell.test.ts; cd packages/server && bun test test/permission-saved.test.ts. session-grant-upstream-reds.test.ts requires exactly these to fail (tool-shell's two pre-existing "conditional substitutions respect once|always" reds tolerated). Rollback: never revert permission.ts alone while the adapter sends always as it is — "allow for this session" would become a permanent project-level approval; revert the I-05 slice as one commit.

entries.decision: A model the user explicitly picked out-ranks a command's or its agent's recommended model (#1560).

mechanism.ladder: L3 (re-taken: the command switches the session model only when the session has none; a subtask child runs on the parent's model before the command's or its agent's. No plugin seam reaches the command's switchModel)

tests.name: a picked session: the command's own model does not switch it; the command still runs
a picked session: the command agent's model does not switch it either
a subtask command: the child session runs on the parent's picked model

entries.note: The pick is the session's `model`. L6 contract: Code Puppy's adapter switches the session model to the composer's pick before every send, so the field always carries the user's choice (orchestrator, plan 6bc34b3ce5). Upstream-native and kept: a session with no model takes a command's model, which then stays the session's model.

entries.decision: A server that cannot start fails with a named cause (workspace_missing / dependency_missing / spawn_failed / handshake_timeout …) (#1563 AC2).

mechanism.ladder: L3 (re-taken packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts names the cause at the source; re-taken index.ts prefixes Mcp.Status.Failed.error with it through withFailureCode, and the L6 adapter reads it back with parseFailureCode — both in packages/schema/src/codepuppy-net-failure.ts; ruling #1666 6756103246 item 2 (b))

entries.decision: A call planned against an MCP tool's definition fails loudly when a later server generation changed that tool; an unchanged definition runs on the new connection (#1563 AC6).

mechanism.ladder: L3 (re-taken: the McpTool call compares the definition it was offered under with the server's current listing after the approval wait, right before the send; re-taken packages/core/src/mcp/index.ts sends the retry after a recovered session only if the tool's definition is unchanged; sameTool from packages/core/src/mcp/codepuppy-first-party-mcp.ts)

entries.decision: An MCP failure's logs and public failed status carry Code Puppy's named cause with the HTTP status or process exit, never the remote server's response body or the local server's stderr (#1645).

mechanism.ladder: L3 (re-taken: safeDescription / safeExplain give logs and the failed status only the HTTP status or the process exit; re-taken connection.ts builds the failed status from it)

entries.decision: A model route whose deployment declared no credential refuses before the socket opens instead of sending an unauthenticated request (#652, owner ruling 2026-07-28 per the v1 source comment).

mechanism.ladder: upstream-native on OpenCode 2: every provider entry resolves its credential with Auth.optional / Auth.config, which fail before the socket opens; pinned

tests.name: the provider entries are enumerated (an empty list would make the pin vacuous)
every provider entry built with no credential sends nothing without one

entries.note: Audit 2026-11-09: all 94 provider entries with a model factory refuse without a credential on unmodified OpenCode 2 routes (7 entries have no model factory; media routes take auth as a required field). The route default (Auth.none) is not re-taken. The engine's keyless inference for a configured provider with no key and no connection (packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts) is kept from an absent BYOK key file by L5's BYOK fix.
